headline: Failed Senate resolution would have canceled the consumer finance agency's withdrawal of a rule on checking lenders for risks to military families.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) action that withdrew an earlier rule. That earlier rule was about the CFPB examining financial companies for risks to active-duty servicemembers and their covered family members. If adopted, the withdrawal would have had no legal effect, and the CFPB could not issue a substantially similar withdrawal without new approval from Congress. No official summary was available, so the details are based on the title.

who_it_affects.group: Active-duty servicemembers and their covered dependents
who_it_affects.how: The earlier rule on CFPB examinations for risks to them would likely have stayed in place instead of being withdrawn.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders and other financial companies that serve military families
who_it_affects.how: They could have remained subject to CFPB examinations focused on risks to servicemembers and their dependents.
Its withdrawal of the rule would have been canceled, and it would have been limited in issuing a similar withdrawal later.
